items.title: Accept or decline the offered daycare place
items.quote: Bitte sagen Sie uns binnen 12 Arbeitstagen ab dem Datum dieses Briefes zu oder ab.
items.computation: The letter is dated Thursday 19.11.2026 and explicitly states the 12-working-day period runs 'ab dem Datum dieses Briefes' (from the date of this letter itself), counting Monday-Friday only, holidays disregarded (none fall in this window in NW anyway). Because the period is tied to the beginning of a named calendar day rather than to an external event (such as receipt), §187 Abs. 2 BGB applies, so the day of the letter (19.11.2026, a Thursday) counts as working day 1. Counting forward, skipping Sat/Sun: 19.11.(Thu,1), 20.11.(Fri,2), 23.11.(Mon,3), 24.11.(Tue,4), 25.11.(Wed,5), 26.11.(Thu,6), 27.11.(Fri,7), 30.11.(Mon,8), 01.12.(Tue,9), 02.12.(Wed,10), 03.12.(Thu,11), 04.12.(Fri,12). That makes the 12th working day Friday 04.12.2026. (Alternative reading under §187 Abs. 1 BGB, treating the letter's issuance as an event and excluding 19.11. from the count, would instead give Monday 07.12.2026.) The earlier, safer date is used here.

warnings: The counting method for the '12 Arbeitstage ab dem Datum dieses Briefes' is ambiguous: depending on whether the letter's own date (19.11.2026) is counted as the first working day (§187 Abs. 2 BGB) or excluded (§187 Abs. 1 BGB), the deadline falls on either 04.12.2026 or 07.12.2026; the earlier date (04.12.2026) was used to be safe, and the user should reply as early as possible well before either date.

This is a private company (a childcare provider), not a public authority, so the statutory 3-day postal delivery fiction for administrative letters does not apply; however the letter sidesteps the delivery question entirely by starting the period from the letter's printed date rather than from receipt.
